objective:
Build core-data's restricted data-layer operations on top of the schema v1 Room database, and prove the integrity rules with host-side tests. After this task the ONLY ways code can write to the database are the operations listed below.

CONTEXT: core-data (package root com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.data) has ActivityLedgerDatabase (core.data.db, version 1, exported schema core-data/schemas/com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.data.db.ActivityLedgerDatabase/1.json), six internal entities in core.data.db.entity (RawCaptureEntity, CanonicalActivityEntity, ActivityAliasEntity, InterpretationEntity, ActivityOccurrenceEntity, CorrectionEntity), EnumConverters, and a TEMPORARY insert-only core.data.db.dao.FixtureInsertDao that exists only for schema tests. IdFactory (fun interface, newId(): String) with UuidV7IdFactory in core.data.id; DeterministicIdFactory in the test source set. Enums from core-domain com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.domain.model (ProcessingState, CorrectionSource, VisibilityStatus, TimePrecision, ActivityState, ...). Tests: Robolectric, @RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class), org.junit.Test + kotlin.test assertions, helper inMemoryTestDatabase<T>() (plain Room in-memory, allowMainThreadQueries; Room itself enforces foreign keys). Existing tests: ActivityLedgerDatabaseToolingTest, SchemaIntegrityTest (uses FixtureInsertDao via test Fixtures.kt), EnumConvertersTest, IdFactoryTest. room-ktx is on the classpath (suspend DAOs, withTransaction/useWriterConnection).

DESIGN (implementation details are your call within these rules):
- Delete FixtureInsertDao. Re-point SchemaIntegrityTest and any other test fixtures to insert rows via raw SQL helpers in the test source set (e.g. through db.openHelper.writableDatabase), so tests can still create states the production API deliberately cannot (e.g. an occurrence with a dangling FK, a HIDDEN occurrence). Keep every existing SchemaIntegrityTest scenario and its assertions.
- Internal DAOs expose only: raw captures - insert, updateProcessingState(id, state, updatedAt) implemented as an UPDATE that touches only processing_state and updated_at, getById; canonical activities - insert, getById; aliases - insert; interpretations - insert, list for a raw capture ordered by created_at; occurrences - getById, latestOccurrenceOfActivity(activityId) returning the ACTIVE-visibility occurrence with greatest occurred_at (null if none); corrections - list for an occurrence ordered by created_at. Occurrence and correction inserts/updates are NOT callable except through the two transactional operations below (keep those DAO methods internal and reachable only from the operations' class, e.g. via a separate internal DAO used only there, or make them part of @Transaction DAO methods - your call, but document it).
- No @Update, @Upsert or @Delete anywhere; no @Query DELETE anywhere; every @Insert uses the default ABORT conflict strategy (REPLACE would silently delete-and-rewrite a row, which is forbidden - a REPLACE on raw_captures would overwrite raw_text).
- An internal operations class (e.g. ActivityLedgerWriter) holding the database and an IdFactory, with:
  (a) acceptInterpretation: inputs are a raw capture id, the interpretation to store (without id, or id assigned by the operation), an optional new canonical activity to create (display name, normalized name), the occurrence's canonical activity id when no new activity is created, occurredAt, timePrecision, activityState, and now. In ONE transaction: if an occurrence already exists for that raw capture, return its id and write nothing at all; otherwise insert the interpretation (its raw_capture_id must equal the given raw capture id - reject otherwise), insert the new canonical activity if given (status ACTIVE), insert the occurrence (canonical activity = new activity if created else the given id; effective_interpretation_id = the new interpretation; captured_at copied from the raw capture; visibility ACTIVE; created_at/updated_at = now), and set the raw capture's processing_state to PERSISTED with updated_at = now. Return the occurrence id. Any failure rolls back everything.
  (b) applyCorrection(occurrenceId, requested changes, source: CorrectionSource, reason: String?, now): requested changes are optional new canonical activity id, occurredAt, timePrecision, activityState, effectiveInterpretationId. In ONE transaction: read the occurrence; for each field whose requested value is non-null AND differs from current, record previous=current and new=requested in one corrections row (fields not changing are null on both sides); update the occurrence's changed fields and updated_at = now. If no field actually changes, write nothing and signal it (e.g. return null or throw IllegalArgumentException - document which). A new effective interpretation must belong to the same raw capture as the occurrence - reject otherwise. Returns the correction id.
- No logging of row contents; exception messages must not include raw_text or other user-entered text (ids and enum names are fine).
- Suspend or blocking DAO functions: your call; if suspend, tests use runBlocking. Report the choice.
non_goals: No schema changes: 1.json must stay byte-identical and the database version stays 1; no new entity, column or index.
No production database builder/factory, migrations list or migration harness (next task).
No domain services, repository interfaces in core-domain, interpretation business validation, temporal resolution, alias promotion, activity merge, visibility change operation, or hard deletion.
No changes outside core-data/src (no build files, catalog, docs, other modules).
No logging of row contents; no ML Kit; no fallbackToDestructiveMigration.
Do not disable, @Ignore or weaken existing tests or assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Correction scenario end to end (TEST_STRATEGY section 8): a raw capture 'I edged the lawn.' is accepted as activity 'Mow lawn'; then applyCorrection changes it to an existing 'Edge lawn' activity with source USER. Assert: raw_text unchanged; the original interpretation row still exists unchanged; exactly one correction row with previous_canonical_activity_id = Mow and new_canonical_activity_id = Edge and other previous/new pairs null; occurrence now points to Edge with updated_at advanced; latestOccurrenceOfActivity(Mow) no longer returns it and latestOccurrenceOfActivity(Edge) does; the occurrence's effective interpretation is still the original interpretation.

Raw text is write-once: a test exercises every write operation the layer exposes (insert capture, updateProcessingState, acceptInterpretation including its retry path, applyCorrection for each correctable field) against one capture and asserts raw_text, source, captured_at and captured_zone_id are identical to the inserted values afterwards.

Structural guard test: reflecting over every @Dao interface/abstract class in core-data main sources (enumerate them explicitly or by scanning ActivityLedgerDatabase's DAO accessors), assert no method carries @Update, @Upsert or @Delete; every @Query whose SQL starts with UPDATE targets only raw_captures (setting only processing_state and updated_at) or activity_occurrences; no @Query starts with DELETE; every @Insert has onConflict ABORT (default). Demonstrate it bites by temporarily adding an @Update method, running the test, capturing the failure, and reverting.

Atomicity: acceptInterpretation given a canonical activity id that does not exist fails and leaves zero new interpretation rows, zero new canonical activities (also when a new activity was requested alongside a failing later step - construct such a case), zero occurrences, and the raw capture's processing_state and updated_at unchanged.

Idempotency: calling acceptInterpretation twice for the same raw capture returns the same occurrence id and results in exactly one occurrence, one interpretation, and at most one canonical activity created by the call pair (the second call supplying a new activity must not create one).

applyCorrection: a no-op request writes nothing (documented behavior asserted); an effective interpretation from a different raw capture is rejected and writes nothing; a multi-field correction records all changed pairs in one row; a USER-source and a REINTERPRETATION-source correction both persist their source.

latestOccurrenceOfActivity ignores HIDDEN occurrences (inserted via test raw SQL), returns the greatest occurred_at among ACTIVE ones, and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for its SQL shows use of index_activity_occurrences_canonical_activity_id_occurred_at (asserted in a test).

FixtureInsertDao is gone; all previous SchemaIntegrityTest scenarios still exist and pass; core-data/schemas unchanged (git diff HEAD -- core-data/schemas empty); no Room/KSP warnings; `./gradlew :core-data:test --rerun-tasks` and `./gradlew test` pass with per-class JUnit XML counts reported.
